lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say the Spanish sounds of table words clearly and greet a host or server politely.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Greet the host with buenas noches, say your name, ask how they are, and say three table words clearly.
lessons.title: Evening Greetings and French Table Sounds
lessons.objective: Greet a host in the evening, introduce yourself, and say common French dinner words clearly.
lessons.focus: Use bonsoir on arrival and vous with an unfamiliar host. Hear the nasal vowel in bonsoir, French u in menu, and the final consonant in fourchette; the final x in choix is silent. Bonne soirée is a farewell, while bonne nuit is normally said when someone is going to sleep.
lessons.scene: Sam arrives at a restaurant in Lyon and greets the host, Camille.

cards.note: At a restaurant, une serviette is a napkin; context distinguishes it from a towel.

cards.en: Very well, thank you. And you?
See you soon, have a good evening!

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Bonsoir. Je m'appelle Sam.
reader.en: Good evening. My name is Sam.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Bonsoir, Sam. Bienvenue au restaurant.
reader.en: Good evening, Sam. Welcome to the restaurant.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Comment allez-vous ?
reader.en: How are you?

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Très bien, merci. Et vous ?
reader.en: Very well, thank you. And you?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Très bien. Je vois la table et la carte.
reader.en: Very well. I see the table and the menu.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Voici une serviette, une fourchette et une cuillère.
reader.en: Here are a napkin, a fork, and a spoon.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Merci, c'est très gentil. De l'eau, s'il vous plaît.
reader.en: Thank you, that's very kind. Some water, please.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Bien sûr. Bon dîner !
reader.en: Of course. Enjoy your dinner!

speaking.goal: Greet the host, say your name, ask how they are using vous, and name a table, napkin, and fork clearly.

recall.cueEnglish: From memory, say the French word for napkin.

hear.cueEnglish: Listen for the French word for fork.

type.cueEnglish: Type the French word for the menu.

write.cueEnglish: Write a polite question asking how the host is.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Give the size of your group, a dinner time and simple quantities of wine, food and pesos.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the host how many people are in your group, what time your reservation is, and order 2 glasses of wine.
lessons.title: Party Size, Reservation Time, and Dinner Quantities
lessons.objective: State how many people are dining, give a reservation time, and order simple quantities in French.
lessons.focus: Use une table pour quatre and nous sommes six for party size. Say a reservation time with à: à vingt heures trente. Deux verres de vin rouge uses de after the measure; une demi-bouteille and un demi-kilo show different forms of demi.
lessons.scene: Sam confirms a reservation for four and asks Camille for wine and a shared dish.

cards.fr: Une table pour quatre, s'il vous plaît.
Ma réservation est à vingt heures trente.
Deux verres de vin rouge, s'il vous plaît.
cards.en: Two glasses of red wine, please.

cards.fr: La bouteille à trente euros, s'il vous plaît.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Bonsoir. Vous avez une réservation ?
reader.en: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Oui. Une table pour quatre, au nom de Sam.
reader.en: Yes. A table for four, under Sam's name.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: À quelle heure est votre réservation ?
reader.en: What time is your reservation?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Ma réservation est à vingt heures trente.
reader.en: My reservation is at 8:30 p.m.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Parfait. Voici la carte des vins.
reader.en: Perfect. Here is the wine list.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Deux verres de vin rouge, s'il vous plaît.
reader.en: Two glasses of red wine, please.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: La bouteille est aussi à trente euros.
reader.en: The bottle is also thirty euros.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Merci. D'abord, deux verres, et un plat à partager.
reader.en: Thank you. First, two glasses, and a dish to share.

speaking.goal: Say how many people are in the group, give the reservation time, and order two glasses of red wine.
speaking.closure: Très bien. Je vous accompagne à votre table.

Deux verres de vin rouge, s'il vous plaît.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Describe dishes, tables and yourself with ser and estar at dinner.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the server where you are from, then say whether your dish is hot, cold, salty or delicious.
lessons.title: Describe a Dish and Check a Table
lessons.objective: Identify yourself, describe a dish's present taste or temperature, and ask whether a table is available in French.
lessons.focus: French uses être in both c'est mon anniversaire and la soupe est froide; it has no ser/estar verb split. Use c'est to identify an occasion and est with an adjective to describe a dish or table. Est-ce que introduces a yes/no question.
lessons.scene: Sam asks for a terrace table and tells Camille about a cold soup and a birthday dinner.

cards.fr: Est-ce que la table en terrasse est libre ?
Est-ce que ce plat est épicé ?
Je viens du Canada et je suis en vacances.
cards.en: I'm from Canada and I'm on vacation.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Bonsoir. Est-ce que la table en terrasse est libre ?
reader.en: Good evening. Is the terrace table available?

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Oui, cette table est libre. Vous êtes d'où ?
reader.en: Yes, this table is available. Where are you from?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Je viens du Canada et je suis en vacances.
reader.en: I'm from Canada and I'm on vacation.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Bienvenue ! Vous fêtez quelque chose ?
reader.en: Welcome! Are you celebrating something?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Oui, c'est mon anniversaire. La soupe est froide.
reader.en: Yes, it's my birthday. The soup is cold.

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Je vais apporter une soupe chaude. Et le poisson ?
reader.en: I'll bring a hot soup. And the fish?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Le poisson est délicieux. Est-ce que ce plat est épicé ?
reader.en: The fish is delicious. Is this dish spicy?

reader.speaker: Camille
reader.fr: Non, il n'est pas épicé. Bon anniversaire !
reader.en: No, it is not spicy. Happy birthday!

speaking.opening: Bonsoir. Est-ce que cette table vous convient ?
speaking.goal: Say where you are from, ask whether the terrace table is available, and describe your dish as hot, cold, salty, or delicious.
speaking.closure: Merci. Je vais m'occuper de votre soupe.

Je viens du Canada et je suis en vacances.

internalReviewNotes: Qualified French review is required for naturalness, register, pronunciation notes, and variant responses before release.
Foundation 2 adapts the source's peso example to euros for the French restaurant scene; preserve the outcome of giving a price and quantity.
Foundation 3 replaces the Spanish ser/estar contrast with French être, c'est, adjective agreement and question formation; the language-specific difference is taught explicitly.
